title: Data Residency + Compliance Discovery - Elk Bank

Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Logging and retention limits for financial PII

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start: 14:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Elk Bank - Head of Cloud), Michael Ortiz (Elk Bank - CISO), Priya Patel (Elk Bank - Lead ML Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed data residency requirements for EU and US, preferences for no PII in logs, potential Dedicated or Private deployment. Next steps: security docs send, architecture call.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samira from Redwood, and with me is Marco, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:05] Laura: Hi Samira, good thanks. Laura here.
[00:07] Michael: Michael on my end.
[00:08] Priya: Priya, hi.
[00:10] Samira: Great. Quick agenda: we want to understand your compliance constraints, what you're evaluating (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and pilot scope. Laura, do you want to kick off with a bit of context?
[00:22] Laura: Sure. We're experimenting with LLM features across customer support and compliance workflows. For pilot, mostly internal tools but eventually customer-facing. Key thing is data residency — customer data for EU customers needs to stay in EU, and we have restrictions on logs, so we can't keep unredacted PII for more than 24 hours.
[00:40] Samira: Got it. When you say logs can't keep PII, is that both request/response and system logs?
[00:47] Laura: Primarily request/response. We can redact on client side, but for some flows the bank wants full request captured for audit for a short period. Also Michael will have specific retention rules.
[00:58] Michael: Yeah, from a security standpoint we need audit trails but PII has to be redacted or encrypted at rest. We also need strong KMS controls and an ability to rotate keys.
[01:10] Marco: Understood. For Redwood Hosted we have EU region endpoints and can limit residency to EU, but logs are stored per our retention policy. We also support redaction hooks and can disable persistent training/retention on a per-customer basis.
[01:25] Priya: Can you elaborate on disabling retention? For model improvements or system telemetry, are requests ever used by Redwood?
[01:31] Samira: Good question. By default, hosted uses telemetry to improve the service but Enterprise customers can opt out. We have a 'no retention' clause for Dedicated and Private. I should note, sometimes our product names get mangled in the transcript, but the capability is there — you can opt out of data use.
[01:48] Michael: If we opt out on hosted, do you still keep logs for debugging? We need a guarantee that PII isn't written in cleartext anywhere persistent.
[01:56] Marco: We can do end-to-end encryption and redaction; for hosted we can also set the logs to be ephemeral and only kept for X hours. For Dedicated, logs remain in your VPC and you control S3 retention and KMS keys.
[02:12] Laura: Ok, so Dedicated means like reserved GPU pool in a region we own? And Private would be on-premise?
[02:18] Marco: Exactly. Dedicated is Redwood-managed infrastructure but isolated for you, with VPC peering options; Private is fully customer-managed control plane — on-prem or in your cloud account.
[02:26] Priya: What's the latency delta between hosted and dedicated in practice? Our SLAs for some flows are <150ms p95.
[02:33] Marco: Latency's mostly a network hop. Hosted EU region tends to be the fastest for quick proofs, but Dedicated colocated in your VPC gives you more predictable p95 because of reduced multi-tenant interference. We have customers hitting sub-100ms p95 with batching disabled and optimized KV cache.
[02:47] Priya: Batching disabled? We care about cost though. How do you recommend cost vs latency tradeoffs?
[02:54] Samira: That's the core of Redwood Optimize — choices like batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles. For financial use-cases you can do small batches to keep latency low and use caching aggressively to reduce cost. Marco can share typical numbers.
[03:08] Marco: I'll put together an initial perf spreadsheet. Also note we support quantized model variants that reduce cost but sometimes impact hallucination rates; that matters for compliance.
[03:19] Michael: Compliance note: we need SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001 evidence, and for some products HIPAA-ish controls because we handle some health info in the app. Do you have HIPAA attestation or BAAs?
[03:30] Samira: We have SOC2 and ISO materials and can discuss HIPAA; for high-reg customers we recommend Dedicated or Private where we can sign a BAA and ensure no egress of data outside controlled boundaries. I'll send the SOC2 report and a security package after this call.
[03:45] Laura: Are your audit logs tamper-evident? We have to produce chain-of-custody for several incidents.
[03:51] Marco: Yes, for Dedicated/Private you can forward audit logs to your SIEM with immutability settings on the storage side. Hosted supports log forwarding as well but you rely on our storage TTLs unless you opt for dedicated retention.
[04:05] Priya: Regarding key management, can we bring our own keys (BYOK) / HSM?
[04:10] Samira: Yes, BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted we integrate with customer KMS in some enterprise agreements — depends on contract.
[04:18] Michael: Network-wise, we need to avoid any traffic crossing US borders for EU customers. Does Redwood support region routing and strict egress controls?
[04:26] Marco: We support smart routing and region pinning, and can lock a customer to EU-only nodes. Fallback policies are configurable but can be disabled so you never route outside allowed regions.
[04:36] Laura: Procurement will want a pricing delta for Dedicated and Private. We need to know minimal commit sizes and sample SLOs.
[04:43] Samira: I'll send a pricing sheet for Dedicated EU capacity and an estimate for Private (on-prem) install. For pilot you can do a limited Dedicated reservation.
[04:52] Priya: Are there limits on redaction rules? We might need custom PII detection rules for account numbers, IBANs, etc.
[04:59] Marco: You can provide regex/PII detectors client-side and we also offer server-side redaction hooks. For complicated tokens like IBANs we recommend client-side masking before call to avoid any risk.
[05:12] Michael: On logging restrictions, we need assurance that even ephemeral logs are not accessible by Redwood staff without explicit request and audit.
[05:20] Samira: Access controls are RBAC-based, and support SSO/SAML. For Dedicated and Private, access is limited to your team unless you request support and we create a temporary access ticket which is logged.
[05:31] Laura: Good. What's the typical timeline to stand up a Dedicated EU instance for pilot?
[05:35] Marco: Usually 2-3 weeks for initial capacity provisioning and network peering if nothing unusual. Private on-prem takes longer because of installation and testing — typically 4-8 weeks.
[05:45] Priya: We will want to run a simple benchmark against our models. Can we get a short perf run?
[05:50] Samira: Yes, we'll schedule a perf benchmark. Marco will run with your sample payloads.
[05:56] Michael: Any known limitations around model variants? We run quantized LLMs in-house already.
[06:00] Marco: Redwood supports quantized variants and kernel selection per hardware. There are sometimes tradeoffs for long-context workloads — we'll surface those in the architecture doc.
[06:08] Laura: For the pilot success criteria, we need: EU data residency confirmed, PII retention <24h with redaction, SOC2 evidence, and p95 latency <150ms for key flows. If those are met we move to procurement.
[06:20] Samira: That's clear. I'll capture that as pilot acceptance criteria.
[06:24] Priya: One more thing: we use a tokenization scheme proprietary to our models — can you host custom models or do you only serve curated model catalog?
[06:33] Marco: We onboard customer models for Dedicated/Private; hosted supports a catalog but for enterprise we can support private model hosting. We'll note that for the architecture call.
[06:42] Michael: Ok, procurement will also ask about indemnity and liability caps — we'll surface that later.
[06:47] Samira: Understood. We'll follow up with legal contacts if needed.
[06:51] [General small talk and wrap]
[06:55] Samira: To recap, Redwood to send SOC2 and security package, Marco to propose architecture and perf numbers, schedule deep dive week of Mar 9, and pricing for Dedicated EU and Private. Any other items?
[07:08] Laura: No, that's good. Thanks.
[07:11] Michael: Thanks everyone.
[07:13] Priya: Thanks.
[42:00] End of meeting.

Notes about transcription: some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate" instead of Dedicated), and timestamps are approximate.
